first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, while two inherited findings indicate that shorter, simpler onboarding produces durable activation and adoption gains. This aligns best with sustainable qualified revenue. Promotional pricing directly addresses competitive pressure but carries documented 30-day retention harm, so it should not take the single experiment slot without stronger evidence that downstream value can be protected.

final.rationale: Run a controlled simplification of the self-serve onboarding flow. Verified evidence shows shortened onboarding improved completion by 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and increased 30-day retention by 3%, directly addressing both current declines. SMB signup simplification also lifted activation and qualified revenue, although its 1% retention decline and lack of replication outside SMB warrant segment-level retention and qualified-revenue guardrails. Promotional pricing is not preferred despite competitive pressure because inherited evidence documents material retention harm.
